item.title: Borrowed Planckian dissipation in magic-angle twisted graphene
item.description: arXiv:2611.12947v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In strange metals, the ratio of the coefficients producing signature linear-in-$T$ resistivity and the logarithmic specific heat is free of the coupling between the electrons and whatever scatters them. In the materials studied so far that coupling is fixed by chemistry. Magic-angle twisted trilayer graphene provides a dial with a displacement field $D$ that breaks the mirror symmetry separating a light Dirac cone from the flat bands, and the Dirac carriers borrow the Planckian self-energy of the flat band with a weight proportional to $D^2+D_0^2$. Resistance curves taken at eight fields are consistent with the field acting on the scattering rate rather than on the number of carriers. The slope in temperature follows $a(1+D^2/D_0^2)$ without the quartic term that a depleting Dirac pocket adds, and the elastic part varies by less than 5\% between 0.20 and 0.30~V/nm while the inelastic part grows 2.5-fold up to 0.38~V/nm. The thermally averaged Kubo formula favors flat-band weight placed symmetrically about the Fermi level over a single level. Borrowed dissipation keeps the bath exponent and transport prefactor of the flat band's own electrons but carries exactly twice their entropy per unit of borrowed coupling whenever the bath has dynamics of its own, so the field-differential ratio is $2\pi^3/21\zeta(3)\approx2.46$ for a conformal flat band and, in a numerical search, at most 2.73 for monotonic bath spectra without a high-energy rate floor. The discriminating test is the entropy measured in steps of $D$.
item.dc:creator: Dino \v{S}krgi\'c, Dejan Stojkovic

item.title: Hidden Spin-Supercurrent Counterflow in Conventional Superconductors
item.description: arXiv:2611.13076v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Resistive spin currents conventionally vary in space through spin relaxation or torque, which removes angular momentum from the transported spin. We here demonstrate a qualitatively different mechanism in a conventional superconductor exposed to a spin-splitting field. Spin injection across a spin-mixing interface activates a spin-supercurrent contribution, allowing the resistive spin current to vary spatially while the total spin current remains conserved. Even without a net spin-bias across the superconductor, finite and oppositely directed resistive and condensate spin currents arise. This produces a hidden spin-supercurrent counterflow with vanishing total spin and charge currents. The mechanism persists away from exact compensation and remains sizable over broad parameter ranges. The counterflow may be accessible through spin-to-charge conversion, either as a modification of the electrical response of spin-Hall injectors or through a local quasiparticle inverse spin-Hall signal. Our results establish condensate-mediated spin-current compensation as a previously overlooked alternative to spin relaxation.
item.dc:creator: Johanne Bratland Tjernshaugen, Jacob Linder

item.title: Neutron Scattering studies of the density dependence of One-dimensional Quantum Fluids
item.description: arXiv:2611.13235v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In previous work, we demonstrated that $^4$He confined within a templated porous material preplated with a noble gas to enhance dimensional reduction exhibits one-dimensional behavior. Neutron scattering revealed that the excitations in confined $^4$He are qualitatively distinct from those in two- and three-dimensional superfluid helium, aligning with quantum Monte Carlo calculations. These simulations suggest that three solid layers form, with a one-dimensional liquid located at the center of the pore. Here, we present neutron scattering results as the filling fraction of the one-dimensional core is varied. We observe that the one-dimensional liquid always forms with a fixed density, even as the pore filling increases. We posit that this is due to the growth of the one dimensional extent of the liquid as the filling is increased, but its density remains unchanged.
item.dc:creator: Sutirtha Paul, Rahul Soni, Garfield Warren, Adrian Del Maestro, Paul E. Sokol

item.title: Optically modulated field-dependent electrical response in a non-collinear antiferromagnet/ferromagnet heterostructure
item.description: arXiv:2611.13351v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The interplay among optical, electrical, and magnetic stimuli offers opportunities to control the functional response of spintronic heterostructures. Here, we investigate the field-dependent electrical response of MgO/IrMn$_3$/Py/Au under radio-frequency (RF) excitation, white-light illumination, and direct-current (DC) bias. Under a 20 MHz RF signal with a nominal power of 2 W, the measured voltage in the dark remains at several tens of nanovolts. Upon illumination with approximately 1 W of white light, a pronounced field-dependent feature emerges around 315--320 Oe, reaching 0.9--1.0 $\mu$V. The illumination-associated differential voltage is approximately 0.95 $\mu$V. A DC current of 1 mA produces a response of approximately 1 $\mu$V, while the simultaneous application of RF, DC, and optical excitation increases the voltage to approximately 1.8 $\mu$V. Magnetic characterization reveals exchange bias with a blocking temperature near 380 K, while electrical resistance measurements show a pronounced dependence on magnetic-field orientation, consistent with the anisotropic response of the heterostructure. These results demonstrate that the field-dependent electrical response can be modulated through combined optical and electrical excitation, involving magneto-optical interactions and spin-dependent transport phenomena, potentially including spin Hall-related contributions and the magnetic spin Hall effect. This work provides insights into coupled optical, electrical, and magnetic-field effects in heterostructures based on non-collinear antiferromagnets and ferromagnetic layers.
item.dc:creator: Adrielson Dias, Andr\'e Jos\'e, Jos\'e Lucas, Rodrigo Cristian, Jos\'e Holanda

item.title: Geometry-Selective Higher-order topological insulators induced by $d_{xy}$ altermagnet
item.description: arXiv:2611.13438v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We show that proximity to a $d_{xy}$-wave altermagnet provides an effective route to engineering boundary-geometry-dependent higher-order topological phases. The boundary geometry plays a crucial role in determining the topological properties: axis-aligned edge states remain gapless, whereas diagonal edges acquire effective masses with alternating signs, giving rise to four corner modes localized at the mass domain walls. By projecting onto the edge-state subspace, we derive the effective edge Hamiltonians for different boundary geometries. Furthermore, $\pi$-flux defects introduced under periodic boundary conditions yield zero-energy bound states localized at the flux cores, providing complementary evidence for nontrivial topology without physical boundaries. The interplay between the Zeeman field and the altermagnetic order drives a topological transition through the closing and reopening of the edge gap, while the bulk gap remains open. These findings highlight the crucial role of boundary geometry in higher-order topology and establish proximity-induced $d_{xy}$-wave altermagnetism as a route to engineering higher-order topological phases.
item.dc:creator: Siyuan Cheng, Yuee Xie, Xiaosen Yang, Yuanping Chen

item.title: Facilitated Relaxation Overrides Energetic Pathways in a Multiphase Square-Kagome Artificial Spin Ice
item.description: arXiv:2611.13500v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Relaxation in interacting many-body systems is typically assumed to follow energy minimization, yet local dynamical rules can determine which microscopic pathways are accessible. In facilitated relaxation, these pathways are enabled or blocked by neighboring configurations. However, isolating such rules in natural materials is difficult because energetics, disorder and dynamics are usually entangled. Here we realize a geometrically tunable square-kagome artificial spin ice-a lithographic nanomagnet array-that provides a clean, designable platform for facilitated relaxation. The array hosts two tunable nearest-neighbor interactions and supports multiple low-energy phases: spin crystal, spin liquid and spin foam. In the spin-foam phase, abundant facilitator configurations allow relaxation to follow Boltzmann statistics. In the spin-crystal phase, by contrast, domain-wall excitations are trapped in non-Boltzmann distributions, although energetically preferred relaxation channels exist. The ordered crystal background lacks the facilitators needed to connect topologically distinct domain-wall classes. These classes are therefore kinetically isolated, as observed in both experiment and Monte Carlo simulation. Our results show that transition-network topology can override energetic relaxation, establishing artificial spin ice as a programmable platform for constrained dynamics and nonergodic relaxation.
item.dc:creator: Wen-Cheng Yue, Zixiong Yuan, Peiyuan Huang, Ziao Wang, Hangyu Liu, Tianyu Li, Nuo-Zhou Yang, Jingyue Gao, Chen Ku, Shuo Song, Jiyao Shang, Yang-Yang Lyu, Yihuang Xiong, Xuecou Tu, Liang He, Xun Cao, Ying Dong, Huabing Wang, Peiheng Wu, Cristiano Nisoli, Yong-Lei Wang

item.title: Magnetization-free quantum anomalous Hall effect in altermagnetic weak topological insulators
item.description: arXiv:2611.13508v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The quantum anomalous Hall (QAH) effect is usually realized through ferromagnetism or magnetic dop ing, which limits material choices and often results in low mobility, disorder sensitivity, and low operating temperatures. Here, we propose a mechanism to achieve the QAH phase without net magnetization, using altermagnetic exchange on a weak topological insulator (WTI). The altermagnetic order selectively gaps the Dirac cone at the Z point, while hybridization between the top and bottom surfaces of the WTI thin film opens a trivial gap at the point, generating a Chern number C = 1 phase with a single chiral edge channel. We verify the topological transition through both a minimal thin-film model and a slab geometry, and compute the associated Hall response. As altermagnets and layered WTIs already exist experimentally, this mechanism offers a promising and experimentally accessible route to realizing QAH phases without magnetic doping or global magnetization. The results indicate that altermagnetic surface engineering may provide a clean and controllable pathway for realizing dissipationless edge transport in layered quantum materials.
item.dc:creator: Yanmiao Han, Yu-Hao Wan, Peng-Yi Liu, Rundong Zhao, Qing-Feng Sun

item.title: Topological flat bands from nonlinear periodic motion
item.description: arXiv:2611.13591v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We use the Lax formulation of classical integrable systems to characterize the topology of nonlinear periodic orbits. For a Hamiltonian system with one degree of freedom, we express the chiral-symmetric Lax operator along a periodic orbit in a frequency basis. Energy conservation makes both bands of the resulting tight-binding model exactly flat. The harmonic oscillator corresponds to a fully dimerized topological Su-Schrieffer-Heeger model, while nonlinearity generates long-range hopping through higher harmonics. In the symmetric double well, the winding number changes as intrawell periodic orbits give way to an orbit spanning both wells, and the zero-energy edge mode of the semi-infinite chain disappears. We derive the edge-mode profile and show that its localization length diverges logarithmically as the separatrix is approached. At the separatrix, the period and the hopping decay length diverge while the band gap remains finite; this singular limit of the periodic motion allows the winding number of the infinite frequency chain to change. Canonical quantization of the Lax operator also connects the chiral winding numbers to supersymmetric quantum mechanics: for a bound system on the real line with simple turning points, their sum over all periodic orbits at a common positive energy equals the Witten index. We also apply the construction to periodic nonlinear waves through traveling-wave reductions. The finite-period winding number becomes undefined in their solitary-wave limits.
item.dc:creator: Urei Miura, Hisao Hayakawa

item.title: Plasmons in bilayer graphene with O-type Kekul\'{e} distortion: Electron-hole asymmetry of the effective interlayer tunneling
item.description: arXiv:2611.13716v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The effective interlayer tunneling (EIT) is a key quantity in determining the out-of-phase plasmons of a bilayer structure. Using the tight-binding model and the random phase approximation, we investigate plasmons in bilayer graphene with O-type Kekul\'{e} distortion. Both O/O and G/O bilayers exhibit strong electron-hole asymmetry in the EIT. For the O/O bilayer, the gap of the out-of-phase plasmon remains almost constant as the electron concentration varies, whereas it increases rapidly with increasing hole concentration; hole doping can also lead to stronger anomalous dispersion than electron doping. For the G/O bilayer, enhancing the Kekul\'{e} distortion $\Delta_0$ can weaken the EIT, as reflected by the reduced interlayer hybridization caused by the lifted layer degeneracy, especially for the electron-doped case. For the electron-doped G/O bilayer, the EIT is almost turned off when $\Delta_0=0.3$ from the perspective of the dispersion. Our results imply that switching the doping type between electron and hole can tune the performance of out-of-phase plasmon-based devices by modulating the EIT.
item.dc:creator: Mingyu Wang, Guodong Yu, Shengjun Yuan

item.title: Floquet first- and higher-order topological superconductors: A review
item.description: arXiv:2611.13804v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The current developments in quantum technologies are deeply rooted in quantum computation, with Majorana fermions and their topological protection expected to play a central role. In this context, topological superconductors (TSCs) provide a promising platform for investigating Majorana modes and their potential applications in topological quantum computation. In dimensions $d > 1$, the spatial localization of topological Majorana modes can be controlled in higher-order topological superconductors (HOTSCs), extending beyond the conventional framework of first-order topological superconductors (FOTSCs). In this review, we systematically survey the diverse landscape of topological superconductivity, ranging from FOTSCs to third-order topological superconductors (TOTSCs), in which the spatial dimensionality of Majorana zero modes (MZMs) is progressively reduced. We demonstrate how periodic driving protocols enable Floquet engineering of all these phases, even when the corresponding undriven systems are topologically trivial. Furthermore, we investigate various driving schemes and explore the interplay among spin-orbit coupling, magnetic fields, magnetic impurities, and symmetry-breaking mass terms in realizing Floquet higher-order topological superconducting (FHOTSC) phases, characterized by appropriate topological invariants. We also provide an extensive discussion of topological invariants capable of distinguishing conventional MZMs from anomalous Majorana $pi$-modes, which emerge at two distinct quasienergies and have no static counterparts.
item.dc:creator: Debashish Mondal, Arnob Kumar Ghosh, Arijit Saha, Tanay Nag

item.title: Hierarchical Topological Protection and Subsymmetry-Driven Edge-State Switching
item.description: arXiv:2611.13839v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We reveal a hierarchy of topological protection in which multiple symmetries and their reduced forms provide distinct mechanisms for protecting topological edge states. In Hermitian Hamiltonians obtained by doubling chiral non-Hermitian systems, a structural and an inherited chiral symmetry provide complementary channels of topological protection. By selectively breaking either symmetry, we demonstrate their distinct roles in protecting edge zero modes, establishing different levels of protection under symmetry reduction. Remarkably, even when both full chiral symmetries are broken, fixed subsymmetry constraints allow the protected zero-mode configurations to switch between opposite edges and change in number across the topological phase boundaries of the symmetry-unbroken system. Our results establish a hierarchical framework for topological protection, revealing a route to controlling edge-state configurations via reduced symmetry constraints.
item.dc:creator: Shu Long, Rijia Lin, Hui-Qiang Liang, Linhu Li

item.title: Chiral magnon Kerr interaction from linear and nonlinear Meissner screening in ferromagnet--superconductor bilayers
item.description: arXiv:2611.13937v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Magnon Kerr interaction showing a dependence of magnon dispersion frequency on its population is a useful functionality for nonlinear and quantum magnonics; its strength and sign depend on magnetic anisotropy, bias, and mode geometry. We here propose to use a superconducting gate to tune the Kerr interaction of magnons in ferromagnetic insulators. Even when the superconductor responds linearly, the frequency shift induced by its reflected dipolar field depends on the longitudinal magnetization. The decrease of this magnetization with increasing precession amplitude therefore produces a Kerr contribution. We go beyond this linear Meissner-screening regime by showing that at finite excitation amplitude, the significant Meissner screening currents reduce the superfluid stiffness, thus enhancing the effective magnetic-field penetration and rendering the Meissner backaction amplitude dependent. This superflow-induced pair breaking adds a second Kerr contribution, controlled by the interfacial superflow relative to the nonlinear screening scale. For yttrium iron garnet gated by dirty niobium, we predict a significant renormalization of the Kerr effect by superconductors, with the resulting Kerr contribution strongly chiral in the Damon--Eshbach configuration. By showing that the linear and nonlinear Meissner screening to the Kerr interaction can be distinguished by varying temperature, our work establishes a route to directional control of magnon nonlinear interactions.
item.dc:creator: Hanchen Wang, Tao Yu

item.title: Frequency Comb as a Probe of Fluctuation Mechanisms in Nanomechanical Systems
item.description: arXiv:2611.13979v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Frequency combs are indispensable in metrology. We show that a frequency comb also probes frequency fluctuations of the system. In our nanomechanical resonator, the comb arises from self-sustained vibrations of a resonantly driven nonlinear mode. The comb lineshapes reveal exponentially correlated (Ornstein--Uhlenbeck) frequency noise. Its correlation time agrees with the independently measured relaxation time of the vibrations. The noise leads to anomalous phase diffusion. Its mechanism is generic: like the comb itself, it stems from the strong nonlinearity of the self-sustained vibrations.
item.dc:creator: Maria Kallergi, Daniel K. J. Bone{\ss}, Maximilian Seitner, Wolfgang Belzig, Mark I. Dykman, Eva M. Weig

item.title: Evidence of anomalous Hall crystals in moir\'e rhombohedral graphene
item.description: arXiv:2611.14067v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: An anomalous Hall crystal (AHC) is a quantum state of matter, in which spontaneous electron crystallization leads to a quantized Hall effect without a magnetic field. The state can emerge in materials with strong Coulomb interaction and large Berry curvatures, such as few-layer rhombohedral graphene. Although the idea of AHCs has been invoked to explain some of the observed Chern insulators in moir\'e rhombohedral graphene (mRG), direct experimental evidence of AHCs has been missing so far. Here, we report experimental evidence of AHCs in hole-doped mRG through combined electrical transport and noise measurements. We identify a series of distinct Chern insulators spanning a broad and continuous range of doping densities incommensurate with the underlying moir\'e lattice; the states exhibit current-induced broadband noise and memory effects as well as pronounced gate hysteresis. Systematic magnetic field, temperature and gate dependence studies further support the emergence of a spontaneously charge-ordered state that acts as a parental state for the observed Chern insulators. The absence of Chern insulators at nearby integer fillings also distinguishes the observed state from the reported reentrant or extended quantum (anomalous) Hall states. Altogether, our results establish experimental evidence of AHCs in mRG and open the door for further exploration of the collective dynamics in this new state of matter.
item.dc:creator: Hongyuan Li, Zuhan Geng, Annika Weber, Chenxi Xu, Yifan Jiang, Jiabin Xie, Lujin Min, Kenji Watanabe, Takashi Taniguchi, Kenji Yasuda, Xiaomeng Liu, Jie Shan, Kin Fai Mak

item.title: End-state-assisted tunneling at a topological insulator STM tip
item.description: arXiv:2611.14155v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Recent spin-sensitive scanning tunneling experiments with topological-insulator tips motivate a microscopic understanding of how tip geometry controls current delivery. We show that topological end states mediate resonant tunneling through the gap opened by interedge hybridization in a quantum spin Hall tip. An asymmetric termination gives oppositely spin-polarized helical paths unequal effective lengths and resonance widths. Within an independent-path description, their transmitted-current imbalance vanishes at a matched resonance and becomes finite away from it. Coupling these directional channels to a $d$-wave altermagnet yields a spin-dependent interference contrast. Hybridized end states along a stepped termination provide multiple tunneling resonances. Our results establish end-state-mediated tunneling as a transport mechanism for STM with strongly confined topological tips.
item.dc:creator: Rui Chen, Jie Zhou, Bin Zhou, Dong-Hui Xu

item.title: Edge quantum weight of finite Chern flakes and its topological floor
item.description: arXiv:2611.14271v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The zero-point energy of a circuit measures the polarization fluctuation of an insulator coupled to it. In a crystal this is the bulk quantum weight $K_\mathrm{bulk}$, which the Chern number $C$ bounds below by $|C|$. We show that a finite Chern flake adds an edge term that survives as the flake grows. The low-frequency transitions of its chiral edge carry a dipole weight, the sum of their squared dipole matrix elements, $K_\mathrm{edge}\geq|C|$ per unit area, a floor that follows from the positive absorption of both circular polarizations by every transition and the known cancellation of circular dichroism between edge and bulk. A weakly coupled circuit slower than the edge modes therefore reads $K_\mathrm{bulk}+K_\mathrm{edge}$, averaged over two field directions, while a faster one below the bulk gap approaches $K_\mathrm{bulk}$, so which quantum weight is measured depends on whether the flake is made large or the circuit slow first. Exact free-fermion calculations on lattice flakes bear out the floor and this dependence on the circuit frequency. The result holds at weak coupling, which a growing flake at fixed coupling eventually leaves. Above the floor, the edge weight of one channel is a number fixed by the shape of the boundary and the edge velocities, which square and rectangular lattice flakes follow to within 0.003. Each further edge channel adds its own such number, while the circular dichroism of the edge counts only the net chirality.
item.dc:creator: Rohit Narula

item.title: Good Practices for Measuring the Interfacial Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya Interaction by Brillouin Light Scattering and Magneto-Optical Kerr Effect
item.description: arXiv:2611.14405v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The interfacial Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya interaction (iDMI) is a key ingredient for stabilizing chiral magnetic states, such as skyrmions and chiral domain walls, which are key building blocks for next-generation spintronic technologies. Despite its importance, the quantitative determination of the iDMI constant, $D$, is often plagued by significant discrepancies. This paper establishes a set of good practices for measuring iDMI using two primary techniques: Brillouin Light Scattering (BLS) and the Magneto-Optical Kerr Effect (MOKE). Through the analysis of Co/Pt-based heterostructures, this work provides a comprehensive roadmap for measurement procedures, data evaluation, and uncertainty analysis. Our analysis highlights the crucial role of magnetic parameters used to extract the iDMI constant and propagation of their uncertainties, and the measurement model for enhancing measurement reliability. The proposed methodology provides a practical framework for improving the consistency and reproducibility of iDMI measurements across different laboratories and experimental techniques.
item.dc:creator: Marco Madami, Silvia Tacchi, Adriano Di Pietro, Alessandro Magni, Giovanni Gandini, Christian Rinaldi, Giovanni Carlotti, Gianfranco Durin, Johannes Hertel, Maximilian Lederer, Christopher H. Marrows, Vito Puliafito, Michaela Kuepferling

item.title: Tuning and Mapping of Two-Tone Optomechanical Instability up to the Physical Limits
item.description: arXiv:2611.14427v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We report on the compete theory describing the two-tone instability proper to optomechanical back-action-evading experiments. We address all possible mistunings (including power imbalance of the two pumps), as well as the device imperfections (finite mechanical quality factor, and sideband resolution). We illustrate the importance of power mistuning and sideband resolution, the latter being particularly relevant in finding the back-action-evading "sweet spot". The model is compared to experiments performed up to an extremely high cooperativity, of almost a 100. This has been made possible thanks to a fine-tuning procedure, which is presented. The agreement theory-experiment is very good, and the limiting factor is unraveled: cavity frequency noise. Besides, we discover at very high drive powers new self-driven states, which all share the characteristic feature of presenting a mechanical comb spectrum; as if the synchronization of the responses to the two drives (which occurs at lower powers) was destroyed by nonlinear effects. We believe that our work is extremely relevant to the implementation of back-action-evading experiments, as well as other related two-tone schemes.
item.dc:creator: Marco Dicosta, Alexandre Delattre, Louise Banniard, Laure Mercier de L\'epinay, Andrew Fefferman, Eddy Collin

item.title: Kinematic Quantum Geometry
item.description: arXiv:2611.13089v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Kinematic quantum geometry describes fast degrees of freedom (DOFs) that adiabatically follow states parametrized by both the coordinates and the velocities of slow DOFs. It extends Born-Oppenheimer geometry, which depends on coordinates alone, introduces mixed Berry curvatures, and modifies the effective theory governing the slow DOFs. We test its predictions in two setups: spinful particles moving in magnetic textures, and Dirac electrons in graphene coupled to an LC circuit. In the first, kinematic quantum geometry produces a velocity-dependent effective mass tensor and generates a Lorentz-like force nonlinear in velocity that can arise even in coplanar textures. In the second, it renormalizes the circuit capacitance and generates a Hall current nonlinear in the electric field. For small velocities, it reproduces recent results for electronic dynamics in external electromagnetic fields and in pseudospin textures. However, the framework can remain valid at large velocities beyond the perturbative regime, provided the kinematic states are sufficiently slowly varying.
item.dc:creator: Bernardo Barrera, Nishchhal Verma, Raquel Queiroz, Anatoli Polkovnikov, Anushya Chandran

item.title: Mimicking the zero-field Josephson diode effect with remanent magnetization and self-field
item.description: arXiv:2611.13157v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: A Josephson junction whose critical current is larger in one direction than in the other is a diode. With a magnetized barrier, a junction can be a diode at zero applied field, and this is commonly attributed to an intrinsic Josephson diode effect, in which the magnetic barrier breaks time-reversal symmetry. Here we show that the same signatures arise from two ordinary ingredients: the magnetic field of the bias current in the electrodes and the remanent magnetization of the barrier. In cross-type Nb/Pd$_{89}$Ni$_{11}$/Nb junctions, the self-field displaces the interference patterns of the two current polarities in opposite directions. An in-plane remanent magnetization translates the pattern and brings the resulting asymmetry to zero field, where the junction mimics a nonvolatile diode with an asymmetry of 10 to 12% and a polarity set by the magnetization direction. Reversing the current or the field cannot distinguish this mimic from an intrinsic effect, but the wiring can: moving the current lead to the other arm of the electrode across the field reverses the self-field diode, in applied field and at zero field alike, whereas an intrinsic diode would be unchanged. This gives a simple dc test for Josephson diodes in the current-perpendicular-to-plane geometry.
item.dc:creator: Nathan Satchell, Arjun Sapkota, Pukar Sedai, Kurt Lorenzen, Juan Gomez

item.title: A Perspective on Topological Charge Density Wave Materials
item.description: arXiv:2611.13360v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Charge density waves are among the earliest known ordered states in quantum materials, yet they have re-emerged at the center of modern discussions of topology, symmetry breaking, and collective dynamics. In several material classes, charge-density-wave order reshapes electronic bands, boundary states, defect structures, and electromagnetic responses in ways that invite a topological interpretation. Real-space imaging has shown that incommensurate order can form networks of phase defects rather than uniform modulations. Boundary-resolved spectroscopy has revealed in-gap modes whose existence and spatial structure track the charge-density-wave order, although such observations remain confined to a single material family. In Weyl materials, density-wave gaps have been linked to axion-like magnetoelectric response, placing the charge-density-wave phase within a dynamical-field description of the effective action. In kagome metals, charge order is intertwined with Berry curvature, unconventional symmetry breaking, and superconductivity. These developments have led to the term "topological charge density wave," but the phrase describes several physically distinct phenomena. We distinguish three meanings: (i) topology of the order parameter and its defects, (ii) topology of the charge-density-wave-reconstructed electronic structure and its boundary modes, and (iii) axion-like electromagnetic response generated by density-wave order. The experimental and theoretical support for these three meanings differs substantially. This Perspective traces the development of these ideas, clarifies the evidence behind each class, identifies unresolved questions and points of debate, and outlines experimental criteria for establishing topology in charge-density-wave states.
item.dc:creator: Chun-Tung Lien, Nidhish Thiruthukkal Puthenveettil, Alexander A. Balandin, Md Shafayat Hossain

item.title: Dynamical Casimir emission from Floquet-driven Landau polaritons: Gauge invariance forbids a superradiant phase transition
item.description: arXiv:2611.14339v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Ultrastrong light--matter coupling of linear systems, such as Landau polaritons formed by a two-dimensional electron gas in a terahertz cavity, is described by the bosonic Hopfield model, and gauge invariance forbids a superradiant phase transition (SRPT). Modulating the magnetic field alone has been predicted to enhance the cycle-averaged coupling and induce a Floquet SRPT. We develop an exact theory of periodically driven Landau polaritons. Including the electric field induced by the modulated flux (Faraday's law), the problem reduces exactly, by Kohn's theorem, to the electronic center-of-mass mode coupled to the cavity, whose Hamiltonian is a sum of squares at every instant. A theorem of Krein then guarantees stability to all orders above a computable drive frequency, the Krein frequency, for which we give a self-contained proof. Below it, the system is stable except within resonance tongues where the drive creates pairs from the vacuum, the dynamical Casimir effect. At high drive frequency the electrons experience the mean field plus a ponderomotive trap (the Fock--Darwin problem), not an enhanced coupling. A gauge theorem excludes a Floquet photon condensate for any band structure, including Kane nonparabolicity, for which we derive a generalized Thomas--Reiche--Kuhn (TRK) sum rule. The predicted transition arises from averaging the coupling in a fixed Landau-level basis, which yields an effective model that violates the TRK sum rule; under driving, gauge invariance also requires the induced Faraday field. The rule to modulate and average the minimal-coupling Hamiltonian, not the parameters of its projection, applies to any linear, minimally coupled system. Instead of an SRPT, magnetic modulation produces dynamical Casimir emission: Faraday-driven polariton--magnetoplasmon pairs at low threshold, and two-color photon pairs with up to 5--10~dB of two-mode squeezing.
item.dc:creator: S. Hughes

item.title: Designing XY and Dzyaloshinskii--Moriya couplings in Majorana Cooper pair boxes
item.description: arXiv:2603.02713v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We theoretically study how to design spin couplings in networks of Majorana Cooper pair boxes (MCBs) connected by multiple normal-metal leads. The inter-box interaction is generated by the conduction-electron-mediated Ruderman--Kittel--Kasuya--Yosida (RKKY) interaction. We show that the connectivity of Majoranas to the leads enables arbitrary types of couplings. As concrete examples, we show the realization of the XY and Dzyaloshinskii--Moriya (DM) couplings, which are difficult to implement in previously proposed MCB-based schemes. The sign and magnitude of the couplings can be tuned continuously via gate-controlled tunneling amplitudes. These results establish MCBs as a versatile platform for engineered quantum spin systems.
item.dc:creator: Manato Teranishi, Shintaro Hoshino, Ai Yamakage

item.title: Supermoir\'{e} reconstruction and domain-resolved valley topology in helical multilayer graphene
item.description: arXiv:2604.19608v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Extending moir\'{e} graphene beyond twisted bilayers, helical trilayer graphene has emerged as a supermoir\'{e} platform hosting topological bands and correlated electronic states. Here we establish a domain-resolved framework for helical multilayer graphene that links supermoir\'{e} relaxation to low-energy electronic structure and valley topology. Real-space lattice calculations show that relaxation reconstructs the system into locally periodic single-moir\'{e} domains, enabling a local continuum description. Within each domain, downfolding the first-shell model yields effective Hamiltonians near the Dirac points that reveal how the low-energy spectrum decomposes into folded Dirac sectors. The resulting valley Chern topology is domain-dependent and includes gate-tunable responses, as independently corroborated by real-space lattice calculations. Our results identify folded Dirac sectors as the organizing principle of thicker helical graphene stacks, with local stacking families determining the band character and valley topology.
item.dc:creator: Kyungjin Shin, Nicolas Leconte, Jeil Jung, Hongki Min

item.title: Heisenberg-Langevin theory of an exciton mirror
item.description: arXiv:2606.12053v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We develop a Heisenberg-Langevin theory of an exciton mirror accounting for the retardation and the long-range electron-hole exchange. The particular case of a single-component exciton gas is analyzed in detail. The optical bistability due to repulsion between the excitons inside the light cone appears to be prone to a modulational instability towards the non-radiative polariton modes. Above the corresponding threshold, the pumped 2D exciton gas acts as an optical parametric generator of twin polariton beams. Conversely, below the threshold, the mirror acquires the phase-conjugating properties.
item.dc:creator: Sergue\"i V. Andreev

item.title: Artificial spin ice on the CaVO lattice: a tricritical bridge from square to kagome
item.description: arXiv:2611.01397v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Artificial spin ices (ASIs) are arrays of interacting nanomagnets in which phase transitions can be imaged and controlled. Studies of the thermodynamic have focused mainly on the square and kagome lattices, and on their variants. Here we study artificial spin ice on the CaVO lattice, formed of squares and octagons. At fixed lattice constant, the ratio $r$ of the square and octagon link lengths tunes the interactions strongly while changing the geometry only slightly. Magnetic force microscopy and Monte Carlo simulations show a continuous bridge from square-ice-like to kagome-like behavior. At small $r$ the system has a single ordering transition, whereas at large $r$ it passes from a correlated paramagnet to charge order and then long-range order. The two regimes meet in a multicritical region, accurately modeled by a Blume-Capel model of the octagon toroidal moments. From this picture, we design a comparative magnetometry protocol that unambiguously separates interaction effects from single-nanomagnet effects in thermally active samples. Finally, the charge-ordered region maps onto a tunable dimer model, with a Coulomb phase and pinch points along the line between two ordered dimer phases. The CaVO ASI thus provides access to a rich phase diagram only through geometric tuning, without requiring extreme experimental conditions.
item.dc:creator: F. Museur, G. M. Macauley, S. Nilsson, V. Scagnoli, P. M. Derlet, L. J. Heyderman

item.title: Field-free transverse response in altermagnet and topological insulator heterojunctions
item.description: arXiv:2611.04937v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We theoretically investigate the transport properties of a topological insulator (TI) connected to two-dimensional altermagnetic (AM) leads in the absence of an external magnetic field. Exploiting the intrinsic time-reversal symmetry breaking of altermagnets, we report the emergence of a field-free transverse differential conductivity in the resulting AM-TI-AM heterostructure. Our analysis reveals that this transverse response is highly sensitive to the orientation of the N\'eel vector: a finite transverse conductivity manifests when the N\'eel vector possesses an out-of-plane component, whereas it strictly vanishes for in-plane orientations ($\theta = \pi/2$) under symmetric chemical potentials ($\mu_t = \mu_b$) due to the restoration of symmetry between the $k_y$ and $-k_y$ momentum channels. Conversely, when asymmetric chemical potentials are applied ($\mu_t \neq \mu_b$), this symmetry is broken, yielding a finite transverse response even for an in-plane N\'eel vector. Furthermore, we demonstrate that while the longitudinal differential conductivity exhibits Fabry-P\'erot-type oscillations as a function of the TI's chemical potential, the transverse conductivity displays a distinct antisymmetric dependence. Notably, the oscillatory behavior of the longitudinal conductivity persists even at finite temperatures. Spatially, the transverse current contribution decays exponentially with position inside the TI region. We also find that both the longitudinal and transverse differential conductivities exhibit periodic oscillations with the junction parameter $\chi_t=\chi_b$. These findings provide a fundamental understanding of field-free transverse responses in spin-momentum locked surface states, highlighting the potential of AM-TI heterojunctions for next-generation spintronic applications.
item.dc:creator: Bijay Kumar Sahoo, Abhiram Soori

item.title: Imaging spin entanglement with a scanning tunneling microscope
item.description: arXiv:2611.10946v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Artificial spin arrays assembled on surfaces enable atomic-scale studies of quantum correlations. Here we establish a hierarchy of connections between spin inelastic electron tunneling spectroscopy (IETS) and entanglement in spin-$1/2$ systems. We first show that the number of spectroscopically active transitions in a spin-$1/2$ dimer serves as an entanglement witness. Using the leading-order tunneling conductance for the tip placed on spin $i$, $dI(i)/dV$, we then relate spectral moments $\mathcal{M}^{(n)}(i)=\int V^n(d^2I(i)/dV^2)\,dV$ to quantum correlations. The zeroth moment probes the one-tangle in systems with a gapped, nondegenerate ground state. For rotationally invariant Heisenberg systems, the first moment yields thermal spin correlators $\langle\boldsymbol S(i)\cdot\boldsymbol S(j)\rangle$, enabling reconstruction of nearest-neighbor concurrence and spatial imaging of entanglement in spin chains. It also provides access to the internal energy and magnetic specific heat, both usable as entanglement witnesses. Applying this approach to experimental IETS data from nanographene spin chains, we find good agreement with theory. We further discuss how the second moment probes longer-range correlations and the inverse moment relates to local spin susceptibility. For spin-$1/2$ trimers, we connect inter-multiplet inelastic spectral weight to genuine tripartite entanglement quantified by the concurrence fill. Finally, we reconcile the local character of IETS with its sensitivity to nonlocal entanglement through an analogy with digital quantum circuits, where Hamiltonian evolution implements multiqubit operations. These results establish IETS as a tool for quantifying and imaging entanglement in engineered on-surface spin systems.
item.dc:creator: J. C. G. Henriques, B. Vi\~na-Baus\'a, I. Brihuega, J. Fern\'andez-Rossier

item.title: Plasmon excitations in monolayer stanene
item.description: arXiv:2611.12212v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Monolayer stanene exhibits strong intrinsic spin-orbit coupling (SOC) and notably distinct low-energy band features involving both $\Gamma$ and K valleys together with strong electron-hole asymmetry among group-IV monolayers. Its plasmonic properties and external-field tunability remain largely unclarified. Here, we systematically investigate its high-energy plasmon structures and low-energy collective excitation modulated by temperature, electrostatic doping and perpendicular electric field. Calculations use a $sp^3$ tight-binding model with SOC and sublattice staggered potentials, combined with the finite-temperature multiband Lindhard function under the random-phase approximation. Besides the $\pi$ and $\pi+\sigma$ plasmon known in graphene/silicene, stanene supports two new high-energy plasmon branches. For low-energy plasmons, thermal excitation extends the accessible energy-momentum range while preserving high quality factors and collective coherence. Electrostatic doping yields distinct plasmon behaviors: moderate doping gives K-valley dominated intraband $\sqrt{q}$ Dirac plasmons; heavy electron doping retains $\sqrt{q}$ dispersion via Drude contributions from $\Gamma$ and K valleys; heavy hole doping triggers interband transitions near the $\Gamma$ point, producing new $\sigma$-$\sigma$ and $\sigma$-$\sigma^*$ interband plasmon modes and complex multi-branch spectra. Furthermore, the perpendicular electric field enables continuous tuning of the $\sqrt{q}$ plasmon via band reconstruction below 0.3 V/{\AA} and induces extra plasmon modes near band-gap closure. These tunable low-energy plasmons span terahertz-to-mid-infrared frequencies, promising for nanophotonic applications.
item.dc:creator: Jia-Hui Qin, Yunhua Wang

item.title: Tuning correlated states in rhombohedral pentalayer graphene with magnetic encapsulation
item.description: arXiv:2611.12281v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Rhombohedral graphene multilayers provide a flexible platform for correlated physics associated with their flat-band electronic structure. While a variety of correlated states appear in these systems as a function of bias and electrostatic doping, promoting specific correlated flavor symmetry breaking states remains a challenge. Here we show that magnetic encapsulation by CrGeTe3 achieves this in rhombohedral pentalayer graphene, by using switchable exchange couplings induced by ferromagnetic substrates. We show that correlations in rhombohedral multilayers at charge neutrality strongly renormalize the exchange proximity splitting,giving rise to collective spin modes whose character is switched by the parallel or antiparallel alignment of the encapsulation. We further show that upon doping of the flat bands, spin triplet f-wave superconducting solutions emerge, whose layer and spin selectivity is controlled by the magnetic encapsulation, hosting in-gap excitations at the edges. Our results establish magnetic alignment as a means to control spin symmetry breaking and unconventional superconductivity in rhombohedral pentalayer graphene.
item.dc:creator: Cuiju Yu, Yitao Sun, Jose L. Lado

item.title: Nonunitary Quantum Criticality Driven by a General Boundary Condition: Exact Solution
item.description: arXiv:2510.15370v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Nonunitary quantum critical phenomena remain largely unexplored, hindered by the scarcity of exactly solvable models and the numerical challenges in non-Hermitian systems. Here we demonstrate that a general boundary condition drives fundamentally new nonunitary boundary quantum criticality in an exactly solvable lattice model. The exact solution yields a closed-form expression for the boundary-induced equal-time correlation function. The algebraic long-distance behavior of the boundary-induced correlation is governed by the single-particle reflection amplitude at the Fermi level, whose anomalous amplification is forbidden in unitary scattering and therefore provides a direct scattering signature of the nonunitary boundary-critical regime. We use the biorthogonal entanglement entropy as a many-body probe of this boundary-critical behavior and find that it retains logarithmic scaling, while the associated effective central charge, continuously tunable by the boundary parameters, changes from real to complex. The real branch admits a unitary defect conformal field theory (CFT) description, whereas the complex branch lies beyond analytic continuation from the unitary theory. These results establish minimal boundary engineering as an exactly solvable platform for nonunitary boundary quantum criticality and provide a benchmark for broader studies of nonunitary critical phenomena.
item.dc:creator: Yao Zhou, Peng Ye

item.title: Designing Strong and Broadband Nonreciprocal Thermal Radiation in Magnetic Topological Materials
item.description: arXiv:2606.14861v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Breaking reciprocity in thermal radiation opens opportunities for energy harvesting, sensing, and thermal management. Traditional nonreciprocal radiative semiconductor devices need external magnetic field. In this work, we predict a series of magnetic topological materials for magnetic-field-free nonreciprocal thermal radiation in the infrared regime, by combining first-principles calculations with Maxwell electrodynamics. We find strong and broadband nonreciprocity in magnetic Weyl semimetals (e.g., Co$_3$Sn$_2$S$_2$), outperforming the conventional semiconductor such as InAs. Furthermore, we propose universal material design recipes: strong nonreciprocity requires a large anomalous Hall response relative to the optical loss, whereas the broadband response favors large optical loss and small dielectric dispersion. Our work establishes a predictive materials-discovery framework and quantitative design rules for next-generation magnet-free nonreciprocal thermal devices.
item.dc:creator: Yiyang Jiang, Yufei Zhao, Linxiao Zhu, Binghai Yan

item.title: Fundamental Relation between Conductance of Biomolecules and the Fukui Function
item.description: arXiv:2607.13309v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We derive the finite-temperature conductance of a molecule coupled to metallic leads using open-system time-dependent density functional theory (TDDFT). Tracing out the phonon bath via Wick's theorem yields an exchange-symmetric collision integral that preserves Pauli exclusion. When internal thermalization is faster than lead escape, as holds in proteins with multifractal orbitals at the Anderson transition, the exchange-correlation kernel projects out of the slow Liouvillian mode, making conductance directly proportional to the finite-temperature Fukui function of conceptual DFT.
item.dc:creator: Gabor Vattay

item.title: Single-molecule strong optomechanical regimes in SERS via hybrid plasmonic cavities
item.description: arXiv:2608.03307v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We identify enhanced strong coherent Surface-Enhanced Raman Scattering (SERS) interactions facilitated by hybridized metallo-dielectric cavities with a resonant fluorescent molecule. By illuminating a detuned electronic transition near saturation via a narrowband hybrid plasmonic mode, we observe enhanced splittings in the Stokes and anti-Stokes spectra, revealing strong optomechanical coupling and nonlinear vibrational modifications at intensities far below irreversible SERS damage thresholds. We compute the second-order photon correlations that allows identifying the nonclassical character associated to these strong optomechanical interactions and SERS configurations that enables them to optically characterize the anharmonic character of the vibrational modes.
item.dc:creator: Miguel \'A. Mart\'inez-Garc\'ia, Johannes Feist, Diego Mart\'in-Cano

item.title: Interface-Controlled Spin-Orbit Torques in Rare-Earth Synthetic Ferrimagnets Probed by Sagnac Magneto-Optics and Harmonic Hall Measurements
item.description: arXiv:2608.18370v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Spin-orbit torque (SOT) provides an efficient route for manipulating magnetization in spintronic devices, and its accurate quantification is essential. Here, we investigate Co/Gd-based synthetic ferrimagnets using complementary magnetotransport and magneto-optical techniques. We use a Sagnac magneto-optical interferometry method to directly quantify current-induced magnetization tilting and extract the damping-like SOT effective field. The Sagnac measurements show good agreement with harmonic Hall analysis across different Co/Gd and Gd/Pt/Co heterostructures, providing a quantitative determination of the damping-like SOT effective field that does not rely on electrical transport signatures. By varying the Gd thickness and multilayer stacking order, we demonstrate that the damping-like torque is strongly influenced by spin transport and angular momentum conversion at rare-earth and heavy-metal interfaces. The observation of a finite torque in Gd/Pt/Co/Pt structures, where conventional Pt spin Hall contributions are expected to compensate, highlights the active role of the Gd layer in SOT generation. Furthermore, interface engineering enables perpendicular magnetic anisotropy in Gd/Pt/Co/Al heterostructures with a 2-nm-thick Co layer, allowing current-induced SOT switching at current densities of 8-10 MA/cm$^2$. These results establish rare-earth-based synthetic ferrimagnets as a versatile platform for engineering spin-orbit phenomena and optimizing low-power spintronic devices.
item.dc:creator: Akilan K, Koral Aykin, Jose-Luis Ampuero, Apurba Maji, Laurent Badie, Stephane Mangin, S\'ebastien Petit-Watelot, Michel Hehn, Andrew D. Kent, J. -Carlos Rojas-S\'anchez

item.title: Deep-UV All-dielectric qBIC Metasurface for Refractive Index Sensing
item.description: arXiv:2611.08733v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: All-dielectric metasurfaces supporting quasi-bound states in the continuum (qBICs) have emerged as powerful platforms for biosensing, yet their operation remains largely concentrated in the visible and near-infrared regimes. Extending these resonances into the deep-ultraviolet (DUV) to probe the intrinsic electronic absorption of biomolecules presents substantial material and nanofabrication challenges. Here, we experimentally demonstrate a hafnium dioxide (HfO$_{2}$) metasurface supporting DUV qBICs in the wavelength range from 225 nm to 340 nm with quality factors reaching 500. We further demonstrate its refractive index sensing capabilities through integration with a microfluidic cell and optical characterization in reflection mode. We show that the introduction of an aqueous buffer leads to a further quality factor enhancement. Achieving a sensitivity of up to approximately 60 nm/RIU and an operational figure of merit of 40 $\mathrm{RIU}^{-1}$, this low-loss HfO$_{2}$ metasurface provides a robust foundation for label-free DUV biosensing.
item.dc:creator: Be\'ata Idesov\'a, Alexander A. Antonov, Lina Rohrer, Leonardo de Souza Menezes, Andreas Tittl, Tom\'a\v{s} \v{S}ikola, Filip Ligmajer

item.title: Hidden Coherence and Controlled Quasihole Motion in a Fermionic Laughlin State on a Superconducting Quantum Processor
item.description: arXiv:2611.10687v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Fractional quantum Hall (FQH) states support fractionalized excitations and geometric phases, yet experimentally resolving the many-body coherence encoded in their wave functions remains challenging. Here, we prepare a three-electron $\nu=1/3$ Laughlin state on the Haldane sphere using seven superconducting qubits and reconstruct its many-body density matrix. Through Read's composite-boson construction, we reveal vortex-dressed coherence that remains appreciable over a larger separation range than electron coherence. The extended profile is suppressed in a Fock-diagonal reference constructed from the measured populations, demonstrating its dependence on off-diagonal many-body coherence. We further prepare a one-flux-added quasihole and characterize its fractional charge response against finite-size benchmarks. Controlled quasihole motion yields an effective geometric-phase signature from the reconstructed dominant-eigenstate trajectory. These complementary measurements provide microscopic access to the coherent structure and quasihole response of a finite fermionic Laughlin state, demonstrating an experimental route to probing strongly correlated FQH wave functions on programmable quantum processors.
